title: Presheaf presentation of a representable pullback
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F,G$ be categories fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes, and let $f:F\to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces, using the based functors and scheme tests of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and the algebraic spaces of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Let $Q:(\mathrm{Sch}/S)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Type}_u$ be any presheaf, and let $g:\mathcal S_Q\to G$ be a based functor, where $\mathcal S_Q$ is its discrete fibred groupoid. Then there exist a presheaf $P:(\mathrm{Sch}/S)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Type}_u$, a natural transformation $a:P\to Q$, and a based equivalence $e:\mathcal S_P\to\mathcal S_Q\times_G F$, such that the first projection composed with $e$ is two-isomorphic over $\mathrm{Sch}/S$ to $\mathcal S_a$. Neither $P$ nor $Q$ is assumed or concluded to be a sheaf or an algebraic space.

proof.text: Write H = Q x_G F. It is fibred in groupoids: pull back the two entries of an object along a base arrow, and lift the comparison isomorphism using the strong cartesian properties. The uniqueness clauses give the universal property of the paired cartesian arrow.

An automorphism in H(T) has identity Q-coordinate. For z in Q(T), test f on the composite h_T -> Q -> G. The automorphism is then an automorphism in that test fibre product, at the object whose h_T-coordinate is id_T. The scheme test is equivalent over the base to an algebraic space, whose fibres are discrete. Full faithfulness therefore makes the automorphism the identity. Quotients of arrows show that H(T) is a thin groupoid.

Take isomorphism classes in every fibre. These class sets are u-small: for each z in Q(T), choose a representing algebraic space A_z for the preceding scheme test. Its sections at T parametrize the classes whose Q-coordinate is z, so the disjoint union of the sets A_z(T), indexed by the u-small set Q(T), surjects onto the class set. Shrink that quotient to Type u. This argument also covers empty fibres and arbitrary total category universes.

Restrict a class by choosing a cartesian lift. Any two choices are vertically isomorphic, so restriction is well defined. The identity and composition comparisons give the strict presheaf laws on classes. Projection sends a class to its Q-coordinate and gives a natural map a.

The class functor from H to discreteModuli P is essentially surjective. An arrow over a base map factors through a cartesian lift; its vertical factor exists exactly when the classes agree and is unique by step 2. Thus the class functor is fully faithful. Choose its inverse over the base using representatives in the exact fibres. This is e. Its counit identifies projection with discreteModuliMap a over identity base maps, giving the required ModuliTwoIso.

lean.statement:
theorem representable_pullback_presheaf_presentation {S : Scheme.{u}}
    {F : BasedCategory.{v₁, w₁} (Over S)} {G : BasedCategory.{v₂, w₂} (Over S)}
    (hF : IsFibredInGroupoids F) (hG : IsFibredInGroupoids G)
    (f : BasedFunctor F G) (hf : IsRepresentableByAlgebraicSpaces f)
    (Q : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (g : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli Q) G) :
    ∃ (P : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (a : P ⟶ Q)
      (e : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli P) (moduliTwoFiberProduct g f)),
      e.toFunctor.IsEquivalence ∧
        Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (e.comp (moduliTwoFiberFst g f)) (discreteModuliMap a))
